daily_brief: Tensions between Washington and Kyiv dominated headlines as President Zelensky arrived in Brussels to rally European support after announcing Ukraine would resume strikes on Russian oil refineries, defying President Trump's demands [BBC, RFI, Financial Times]. Trump responded sharply, calling Zelensky 'more difficult to deal with than Putin' and labeling the renewed attacks 'a disgrace' [BBC]. EU leaders closed ranks around Ukraine, with Commission President von der Leyen pledging to maintain sanctions and increase pressure on Moscow [Financial Times, BBC]. Meanwhile, ship attacks near the Strait of Hormuz reached record highs as the US-Israeli conflict with Iran intensifies, with 12 vessels reporting strikes in a single week [BBC]. A tragic school shooting in Bend, Oregon claimed the lives of three children and a teacher before an armed bystander killed the 16-year-old attacker [BBC, Le Monde, France 24]. In diplomatic developments, China's foreign minister urged Israel to halt West Bank settlement expansion, calling the Palestinian question 'the greatest historical injustice of this century' [BBC]. Guinea-Bissau denied approving a controversial hepatitis B vaccine trial promoted by RFK Jr., contradicting earlier reports [The Guardian].

top_stories.headline: Zelensky Defies Trump, Resumes Strikes on Russian Refineries as EU Leaders Rally Behind Ukraine
bullets: Ukraine resumed drone strikes on Russian oil refineries after a three-day pause requested by President Trump, with Zelensky stating Moscow never stopped attacking Ukrainian energy infrastructure
Trump called the renewed strikes 'a disgrace' and said Zelensky is 'more difficult to deal with than Putin' in an interview with Newsmax
EU leaders at the Brussels summit pledged to maintain sanctions on Russia and increase pressure, with von der Leyen stating 'we will not lift any sanctions unless Russia stops the war'
Ukrainian defense sources reported Starlink satellite service functionality had been partially restored after apparent restrictions hampered military operations

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Balanced coverage focusing on diplomatic tensions and military implications

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Emphasized European support for Ukraine and Trump's sanctions easing as context

sources.name: Financial Times
sources.framing_note: Focused on EU solidarity and Trump's 'fuel deal' with Moscow

top_stories.headline: Three Children and Teacher Killed in Oregon Elementary School Shooting
bullets: A 16-year-old shooter forced entry into Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon by firing at locked doors on Thursday afternoon
Three children aged 5, 8, and 11, along with one teacher, were killed; a 7-year-old and another teacher remain in critical condition
An armed community member pursued the attacker into the school and shot him dead; police arrived three minutes later
The shooter was a local teenager with no confirmed connection to the school; the motive remains under investigation

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Detailed factual reporting on timeline and victims

top_stories.headline: Ship Attacks Near Strait of Hormuz Hit Record High as Iran Conflict Escalates
bullets: Twelve vessels reported attacks between October 5-11, the highest weekly total since the US-Israeli war with Iran began, with six ships struck in a single day
Oil shipment recovery through the strait has slowed as attack frequency increased, according to industry data
Experts say Iran is attacking ships to assert control over the waterway as the US military increases escort operations for tankers
Attacks are also occurring further from the strait as Tehran expands its targeting range

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Data-driven analysis from BBC Verify with detailed timeline

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Focused on Houthi weapons capabilities and Saudi Arabia interceptions

top_stories.headline: Guinea-Bissau Denies Approving RFK Jr.-Backed Vaccine Trial in Newborns
bullets: Guinea-Bissau's health minister stated the government never authorized the controversial hepatitis B vaccine trial, contradicting earlier reports of approval
The study, championed by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., would withhold hepatitis B vaccines from some newborns to track 'nonspecific' health outcomes
A Danish research ethics committee had voted to proceed based on information that Guinea-Bissau had approved the trial
Critics have called the trial ethically problematic, with one physician stating Kennedy is 'taking advantage of a developing country'

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Critical framing emphasizing Kennedy's anti-vaccine history and ethical concerns; published both the initial approval report and the denial

top_stories.headline: China Demands Israel Halt West Bank Settlements, Positions as Middle East Mediator
bullets: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told Israeli President Isaac Herzog to stop 'forced establishment' of settlements and reverse actions in the West Bank
Wang called the Palestinian question 'the greatest historical injustice of this century' during a meeting in Azerbaijan
China emphasized opening humanitarian access to Gaza as the 'immediate priority' and expressed willingness to facilitate dialogue
Beijing has been positioning itself as a regional mediator, having brokered the 2023 Iran-Saudi diplomatic restoration

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Neutral coverage of diplomatic exchange and China's mediation ambitions
